description:
Investigative journalist Janine Roem delves into the concept of financial cancel culture and its connection to surveillance, control, and censorship. She discusses how traditional mechanisms of financial surveillance are transitioning to newer forms of money like Bitcoin, and highlights the value of sovereign money in this context. Roem explores different interpretations of cancel culture and its association with ostracism and boycotts. She also discusses examples of financial cancel culture, such as the targeting of sex workers, activists, and organizations accepting cryptocurrency. Roem stresses the need to expose and protest against increasing financial surveillance and exclusion, while also examining the intersection of blockchain analysis and surveillance. She raises concerns about privacy and provides suggestions on protecting it when dealing with cryptocurrencies. Overall, the video sheds light on the complexities and consequences of financial cancel culture and more...

Topic: Financial Cancel Culture
Guest: Janine Roem
